$comment: The aura ramp. SEMANTICS ONLY — no hex values live here. The hexes are
in css/tokens.css (--color-aura-red and siblings) and are joined onto
this map by scripts/generate.mjs, exactly as gems.json is joined. Read
dist/tokens.json for the joined result.
⚠️ THIS IS A RATE MAP. A colour here means a POSITION — how fast a
person's gratitude is circulating — not a medium (that is gems.json)
and not a domain (that is tlds.json). Three palettes; seven, seven and
six; and the hues rhyme because a colour wheel is small. Never present
any two of them as one system.
⚠️ THE SEVENTH IS VIOLET, NOT DIAMOND. This ramp and the gem palette
both have seven stops and they are DIFFERENT SETS: this one carries
indigo and ends at violet; the gems carry no indigo and end at the
unrefracted diamond. The shared count is a coincidence.
⚠️ DISCRETE, NOT CONTINUOUS. colorFor() returns a bucket NAME, so a
person is in exactly one stop and never between two. That is what
makes seven flat tokens the right shape here. The Metta Light — the
gem-order descent named in gems.json — is the continuous one, driven
by a single 0-to-1 scalar. Do not build this one as a gradient.
auras.meaning: Circulation velocity, computed as crossings per month over a rolling window and bucketed server-side.
auras.source: thank.heartbank.org/functions/src/auras/compute.ts — COLOR_BUCKETS is canonical for the thresholds; this file is canonical for the colours.
auras.twoRings: A person carries TWO auras at once — one for Kiitos (gratitude shown) and one for Kiitti (kindness given). Same ramp, two independent positions.

$comment: HOW THE RAMP IS WORN. Extracted from thank.heartbank.org's
aura-avatar component, which stays canonical for the
IMPLEMENTATION; this block is canonical for the INVARIANT.
No values here either — the reference size and base ring width
belong to the consumer. What is pinned here is the shape and the
one property that must not be lost when a second surface renders
an aura.
geometry.innerRing: Kiitos — gratitude shown. A border on the photo circle.
geometry.outerRing: Kiitti — kindness given. Outside the border. A FAMILY avatar carries the outer ring ONLY; a person carries both.
geometry.diameterParity: ⭐ THE INVARIANT, and it is what stops an aura becoming a rank: an avatar's visible total is ALWAYS its declared size plus two base ring widths, whatever the amplitude. A wider ring shrinks the PHOTO; it never grows the avatar. Two people rendered at the same size occupy the same space, so no reading of the geometry makes one of them larger. This is a PROPERTY — remove the enforcer and it still holds, because the arithmetic has nowhere to put the extra width.
geometry.amplitudeIsOptIn: Ring WIDTH carries amplitude only where a surface opts in. The default is width from size alone, so intensity is carried by COLOUR ONLY. Where amplitude is on, each ring is capped as a fraction of size so the photo stays the dominant element.
geometry.honestLimit: ⚠️ Parity bounds the FOOTPRINT, not the comparison. With amplitude shown, two rings side by side still differ visibly in width, and width is still legible as more-or-less. The Zero-Point Game's amplitude seam is NARROWED by this, not closed — that seam remains open and is held by the anti-ranking rules, which are rules and not properties.

$comment: NOT AN EIGHTH STOP. This is the absence of a position, and it
must not be reachable by bucketing — nothing computes it.
noReading.rule: ⛔ A person with no computed aura — never active yet, or a read that FAILED — must NOT be painted at the ramp's floor. Red means measured-and-slow; absence means nothing was measured. Collapsing the two makes the surface assert a fact no computation produced, and it renders the person at their floor to do it.
noReading.whyItMatters: The compute side already honours this on the way IN: a hover at zero counts only while the participant is ACTIVE, because the measure is meant to say 'I keep passing on what I receive' and never 'I hold nothing and do nothing'. A client that paints absence as the floor hands that back.
noReading.treatment: A neutral, NON-CHROMATIC ring that keeps its geometry, so diameter parity is preserved and nothing is painted. Grey — never black or white: each of those goes loud in one theme and vanishes in the other, so the same absence would read as emphatic on a light ground and absent on a dark one. White additionally collides with the diamond gem, a deliberate cool near-white that already means a medium.
noReading.values: Held by the consumer, per this file's no-hex rule. The reference implementation reuses the greys its avatar already uses for the anonymous state, so the vocabulary for 'we are not telling you about this person' is reused rather than invented.

buckets.name: indigo
buckets.note: ⚠️ FOUR SHIPPED SURFACES RENDERED THIS BUCKET IN PINK — members-panel.ts, seed, thank and timelog reached for bg-pink-100/text-pink-400 while the three hex maps said #4f46e5. Pink is reserved by construction for B-Dating and must not appear on a Phase-1 surface. Corrected to indigo. If the reason was that blue-indigo-violet are hard to tell apart at tint weight, the fix is to widen the ramp here, where one change reaches every surface — never to borrow the reserved hue on four of them.

reserved.pink: ABSENT HERE FOR THE SAME REASON IT IS ABSENT FROM THE GEMS — held for B-Dating and romantic contexts. This ramp is where the reservation was actually being violated.

collisions: Both are coincidence, not kinship. Three names, three meanings; do not alias them, or re-tuning one will silently move the others.

$comment: The six-TLD rainbow. NAMES ONLY, AND THAT IS THE POINT — unlike gems.json
and auras.json, this file has no sibling hexes in css/tokens.css to be
joined against, because none have ever been assigned. The corpus fixes the
six COLOURS as words (brand-identity-as-architecture §6.4 and §10.1,
resolved 2026-06-30); no file in the estate fixes a value.
⛔ DO NOT PIN HEXES HERE TO MAKE THE PAGE PRETTIER. Nothing consumes them:
the four sites that vendor this layer are sayyourname, playsey, seysays and
333.eco, and not one of them is a heartbank.{TLD}. Six tokens would ship
byte-identical into all four behind brand.lock, buy nothing, and invite
exactly the misuse the gem warning already forbids. Pin them when the first
heartbank.{TLD} surface actually needs them, and measure contrast then —
the gem palette's own hexes were proposed in a working document and lived
there for weeks before they were ratified into tokens.css.
⚠️ THIS IS A DOMAIN MAP. A colour here means a DOMAIN's product class and
its heart-idiom — not a medium (gems.json) and not a rate (auras.json).
The six hues are one-for-one with the six saturated gems, which is exactly
why they are rendered on a different CARRIER on the guidelines page: gems
are chips, these are marks. Same hue, different object, no fusion.
`cssNamed` below is the CSS keyword that spells the doctrine's word. It is
a RENDERING OF THE NAME, never a pinned value — that is why it is a
keyword and not a hex, and why it is allowed to look untuned beside the
measured gems.
tlds.order: Spectrum order, red through violet. The assignments were made per-domain, one at a time, by heart-idiom — that they compose a complete rainbow was found afterwards, and showing them out of spectrum order would hide the only property that makes the allusion earned.
tlds.scope: HeartBank® — one body of five. This palette is body-scoped in a way the gems and the aura ramp are not; it is documented here because the brand layer is where the three palettes are told apart, not because the institution's colour system is one body's domain map.

$comment: ⚠️ CANDIDATES, NOT TOKENS. `pinned` above is still false and these
are deliberately NOT in css/tokens.css — the gate in the top
comment is not met: no heartbank.{TLD} surface vendors this layer
yet (roadmap A187), so twelve tokens would still ship dead into
all four consumers behind brand.lock. This is the working-document
stage the gem palette went through, named in the comment above.
⭐⭐ THE MEASUREMENT CHANGED THE SHAPE, and that is the finding: a
SINGLE value per TLD CANNOT WORK. Measured against the two grounds
the mark actually sits on, three of the six gem hues fail one side
— ruby 2.50:1 on dark, citrine 1.86:1 on white, sapphire 2.05:1 on
dark — and so does what ships today (gold 1.40:1 on white, aqua
1.25:1, darkorchid 2.57:1 on dark). Pinning six values would have
baked in three failures. The six-TLD rainbow needs LIGHT/DARK
PAIRS, exactly as Tier B already does for every other ground-
dependent value, and for the same reason --accent-ink records: no
formula picks correctly, so measure and pin per theme.
⛔ THE PAIRS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. Every light value fails on
the dark ground and every dark value fails on white (all land
1.86-3.26:1). That is what makes the pair structural rather than
decorative — using one value for both themes is the defect.
Hues are the six saturated gems, per the note above; three pairs
keep the gem hex unchanged on one side, so these are minimal
deviations and not a new palette. ⛔ Same hue, different object,
still no fusion: a gem means a MEDIUM, this means a DOMAIN.
RATIFYING THEM means: move to css/tokens.css as --l-tld-<hue> and
--d-tld-<hue>, resolve to --tld-<hue> in BOTH theme files, flip
`pinned` to true, and UPDATE THE README TRIPWIRE, which currently
asserts `grep -o -- '--color-tld' css/tokens.css` must be 0.
candidateValues.method: WCAG 2.x relative luminance. Target 4.5:1 — the mark substitutes for a letter inside a word, so it is read as a letterform and not as a decorative logotype, and the letter-grade threshold is the honest one. (A logotype is formally exempt from contrast requirements; the substitution is what removes the exemption in practice.)

motion.signature: Cardiac morphology: two UNEQUAL beats then a long rest — systole, a weaker diastole, then most of the period at rest.
motion.notRate: The RHYTHM is the signature, NOT the cadence or the amplitude. ~40 BPM at 1.5s ships; a 72 BPM variant was built and rejected. A published spec once claimed ~72 BPM / ~8% expansion — that claim was reframed, not the code.
motion.rest: The diastolic rest is IN THE KEYFRAMES (70%->100%, 450ms of every 1500ms), recurring on every cycle. It is not --beat-delay, which is a CSS animation-delay and fires once before the first iteration only. Both produce stillness; only the keyframe rest is part of the rhythm.
motion.startDelay: --beat-delay is 0s as of v1.3.0. It was 1.5s, which bought nothing recurring and left a Proof-of-Humanity signal motionless for a beat and a half after paint. The token is kept for per-instance STAGGER, so several marks on one screen need not beat in lockstep.
motion.reducedMotion: Stop, and substitute nothing. The static mark is already a meaningful state.

mettaLight.$comment: The session descent. css/metta.css is OPT-IN and is not vendored by a surface with no session.
mettaLight.api: The app sets --t (0 at session start, 1 at session end) on an element carrying the .metta class. Everything downstream reads --metta.
mettaLight.stops: The B-Gem order, ruby to diamond. Seven stops, six segments; stop i sits at t = i/6.
mettaLight.notAnimated: --metta is COMPUTED, never animated. An @property-registered custom property interpolated by @keyframes is the obvious build and is broken in the configuration this feature requires: Chrome does not reliably re-rasterise an element for an animated custom property it INHERITS, and the failure is invisible to getComputedStyle. Six color-mix() steps weighted by clamp() windows instead — no registration, no keyframes, no ticker.
mettaLight.classScoped: The chain is declared on .metta and NOT on :root. Custom properties inherit their computed value, so a chain on :root resolves once against root's --t and descendants inherit a frozen colour. The element that sets --t must carry the chain.
mettaLight.guards: No numerals, no totals, no streaks, no ranks. The light carries the whole signal; --t is an input, never a readout.
mettaLight.breathNotHeartbeat: The lamp's swell is a symmetrical breath with no claim attached. The heartbeat is a Proof-of-Humanity signal with a placement rule. Never give the lamp .beating, and never give a mark the breath. Under reduced motion the breath stops and the COLOUR DOES NOT — freezing the descent would misreport where the sitter is.
mettaLight.nativePorting: Same seven stops, same single scalar: interpolate the gem list at t. That is why it belongs in platform-native animation rather than a library.

--accent-soft on a light ground — the generic oklab mix does not always clear 4.5:1. Measure and pin.

mark.name: B-Emblem™
mark.shape: A universal heart rotated 45° clockwise. Bistable — heart AND capital B, both immediately apparent. Not a reveal.
rules: Inline in the DOM. Never — CSS cannot reach inside an .
The 45° rotation is baked into the path coordinates. Never a transform attribute.
`.beating` goes on CHROME and never beside a person's name.

geometry.$comment: MEASURED with getBBox() on 2026-09-20, not assumed. Two separate facts, and every call site in the estate had inherited both.
geometry.notFilled: The path's bounding box is 18.0828 x 18.0851 inside the 24 x 24 viewBox, so the mark paints across 75.34% of its own square. An <svg> sized 1em therefore paints a 0.753em mark, and the heartbeat's 1.3 peak lands at 0.979em — the box almost exactly. That is why the beat READ AS GROWING TO FIT its slot rather than growing beyond it, and why the rest state looked like the shrunken one.
geometry.notCentred: ⚠ The bbox origin is (3.6824, 2.2349), so the mark sits HIGH and RIGHT in its viewBox and the four insets above are four different numbers. Symmetric margins cannot square it up, and a hand-tuned vertical-align cannot land it: while the svg box is taller than the text, the mark DRIVES THE LINE BOX, so moving it moves the baseline with it (measured slope -0.39 per px, not -1).
geometry.fix: One move: pull the MARGIN box in to the painted mark on all four sides by its own four insets. Then (a) the inline footprint IS the mark, so no phantom padding; (b) the line box sees the mark's height rather than the larger svg box; and (c) an <svg>'s baseline is its bottom margin edge, which is now the mark's own bottom — so plain `vertical-align: baseline` lands it on the text baseline with no fudge factor. Measured after: 0.00px, footprint/mark ratio 1.0000, beat overflowing by exactly 30%.
geometry.neverTransform: ⛔ Do it with the BOX, never with transform: scale(). A CSS animation on `transform` overrides a non-animated one, so `.beating` would silently eat the correction — the same trap the 45-degree rotation is baked into the path coordinates to avoid.
geometry.opticalSize: ⭐ Separate from the fix and a free choice, because 'fills its footprint' and 'sits on the baseline' both hold at ANY size — every margin is derived. Compare against CAP HEIGHT, never the em box, which includes ascender and descender room no capital beside it uses. The mark stands in for a letter B, so it should occupy a letter's space: brand.333.eco ships 0.7534em = 104% of cap, which gives the ~4% overshoot a round/pointed shape needs to read the same size as a flat-topped capital. 118% reads as a logo dropped into a word; 138% swamps the letters and the ® with them.
geometry.flexIsDifferent: ⭐ This is the BASELINE composition — the mark inside a word. A chrome lockup that sets the mark beside a label in `display: inline-flex` with `align-items: center` is a DIFFERENT and also-correct convention: it centres the mark on the text's cap band rather than seating it on the baseline, and needs none of the margin work. brand.333.eco's own header does this and measures within 0.8px. ⚠ Do not 'fix' one to look like the other, and do not probe a flex lockup with an inline-block — it becomes a flex item and reports a position that is not the baseline.

states.static: Proof of Coordinate ℠ — a meaningful state, not a degradation.
states.beating: Proof of Humanity ℠ — but only where the beat can be verified. Ambient institutional beating claims 'humans run this', not 'this person is human'.

$comment: The composition has an internal short-name as of 2026-09-20: B-Wordmark
for the mark-in-word, B-Slogan for the sentence. Internal only — the
® rides on HeartBank and neither short-name carries a mark of its own.
There is NO wordmark asset and there must not be one. The moment this
ships as an SVG a consumer takes the SVG, and the colour stops
inheriting — the same defect causes for the mark itself.
It is a COMPOSITION of files a consumer already holds: emblem.ts for
the glyph, tokens.css for --emblem, motion.css for .beating, and the
site's own i18n for the words. brand.333.eco/wordmark/ renders it.
wordmark.division: Bank = what accumulates is the RECORD of appreciation. Heart = what circulates is the VALUE.
wordmark.substitution: Wherever possible the B in 'Bank' is replaced by the B-Emblem — 'Thank with Heart3ank®'. Only the B in Bank, never the T in Thank.
wordmark.plainText: Heart3ank®. The stand-in is a 3, NOT a heart character: the mark is bistable as a heart AND a capital B, and ♥ keeps only the half that does not carry the letter. (It is also why the estate's shorthand for HeartBank® is H3.) A literal B remains correct where a 3 would read as a digit — a legal instrument, a form field, anything parsed by machine.
wordmark.registrationSymbol: Drawn at full cap height by every typeface: correct at body size, too heavy at display size, where it competes with the mark it defers to. Scale it optically in display settings only; a call site at ~1rem needs no special treatment.
